contexts.text: Woe to them that are with child... ()... Woe is a form of expression which = the danger of eternal damnation. AE 710:7, Explained.

Saying with a great voice. Woe, woe, woe to them that dwell upon the earth () = the deepest lamentation over the condemned state of (such) in the Church... Woe = lamentation over the evil in anyone, thus over his unhappy state... and the triplication makes it superlative. ( = grievous lamentation over the changes of state of the Church at its end... AE 531.)
That woe = lamentation over the present or future calamity, unhappiness, or condemnation of others. Illustrated. AE 531:2. AE 531:3.
One woe is past; behold, there come two woes more hereafter () = further lamentations over the devastation of the Church. AE 564.

The second woe is past; behold, the third woe Cometh quickly () = lamentation over the perverted state of the Church, and finally a last lamentation, of which below. ( = lamentation over the final vastation of the Church, now certainly at hand. AE 680.)

Woe to the inhabitants of the earth and of the sea () = lamentation over those who are in the internals and externals of the doctrine of faith alone... ( = lamentation over those who become merely natural and sensuous. AE 752.)

Alas! alas! that great city Babylon () = grievous lamentation (over) that religiosity... As woe = lamentation over future calamity, unhappiness, and damnation, Woe, woe (or Alas, alas) = grievous lamentation. AR 785. AR 788. AE 1134. AE 1176.
Woe to the refractory sons () = lamentation over the condemnation of those who avert themselves.
Woe is me... I am become as the gatherings of the summer, as the gleanings of the vintage () = grief on account of the vastation of good and of the derivative truth in the Church.
Woe, woe = lamentation, when it is said Woe! (or Alas!) that city; but it = a curse when it is said Woe to that city.
